acceptance_criteria.description: A Windows launch supplied the standard MCP SDK restricted environment reconstructs exactly the approved minimum keys needed for safe process creation, with deterministic provenance and no arbitrary environment widening.
Missing, blank, conflicting, denied, secret-bearing, unresolved, or unsafe source values still produce an incomplete or rejected result and cannot synthesize an executable launch.
Focused environment and Windows launch regression tests pass and cover the standard restricted-stdio environment plus fail-closed counterexamples.
The clean real Tinto managed stdio probe reaches READY, returns bounded observation evidence, closes successfully, and leaves no owned process, session, runtime-overlay, or artifact residue.

closed_decisions: The root diagnostic proved the same clean real Tinto copy reaches READY through SessionManager when the server inherits the full Windows environment.

The standard MCP SDK stdio transport intentionally passes a restricted Windows environment containing SystemRoot, Path, TEMP, and USERPROFILE but omitting ComSpec, PATHEXT, and TMP; Pumarejo currently rejects that environment as incomplete before process spawn.
Use the existing injected operating-system environment seam and fixed safe defaults only; do not accept arbitrary registry paths, command text, environment keys, or secret-bearing values.
Preserve the fixed Windows minimum, case-insensitive key identity, allowlist/denylist behavior, bounded portable expansion, and incomplete result when the minimum cannot be safely established.
Do not alter public MCP tools or dialog behavior.

focused: pnpm vitest run tests/unit/windows-environment.test.ts tests/unit/launch-environment.test.ts tests/unit/mode-config.test.ts

forbidden_changes: Do not edit files outside the seven owned files.

Do not change public MCP tools, schemas, dialog behavior, provider protocol, Tinto source, dependencies, manifests, lockfiles, queue state, blockers, release files, commits, branches, Jira, or pull requests.

Do not copy the unrestricted parent environment, admit arbitrary environment keys, read arbitrary registry paths, invoke a shell, or weaken secret-key, secret-value, path, executable, custody, cleanup, or loopback checks.
Do not add absolute machine-specific paths or weaken the failure mode when SystemRoot, Path, TEMP, USERPROFILE, or executable identity cannot be proven.
objective: Restore managed Windows launch from the standard MCP stdio restricted environment by reconstructing only the fixed safe minimum launch environment through the existing platform seam, while preserving fail-closed handling for missing or unsafe sources and proving the clean real Tinto stdio launch reaches READY and closes without residue.
